newsitem.title: CANADA: Alliance purchase doubles newsprint output.
newsitem.headline: Alliance purchase doubles newsprint output.

text.p: The acquisition by Alliance Forest Products Inc of Kimberly-Clark Corp's Coosa Pines facilities for US$600 million would double the size of the Canadian forest products firm.

Alliance, which was created in 1994 when Domtar Inc spun off its newsprint and uncoated groundwood papers division, already produces 335,000 metric tons of newsprint annually. The Coosa Pines acquisition adds another 334,000 tonnes of annual newsprint production.
Alliance's agreement announced on Monday to buy Coosa Pines will double Alliance's annual sales to about C$1 billion.

Alliance produces its newsprint at two mills located in the Canadian province of Quebec. Alliance has been converting conventional newsprint machines at the mills to produce higher valued added specialty papers such as those used in making shopping flyers, inserts and certain magazines.

Jim Rowland, publisher of the Canadian Paper Analyst, an industry newsletter, said that despite its doubling of size, Alliance will still be dwarfed by Canada's larger newsprint makers such as Abitibi-Price Inc, which has annual sales of about C$2.7 billion.
"In newsprint, Alliance would still be a mid-size player," Rowland said.
Rowland said that given the falloff in newsprint prices over the last year, he expects more such merger and acquisition activity in the North American industry.
